title: Operational flight plan: Stability debrief and SLO experiment slate (Q3 2026)
content:
Purpose
- Short: capture learnings from recent incidents, run a set of targeted experiments to harden model-serving SLOs, and produce operational changes that are low-friction to deploy.
- Longer: turn incident postmortem findings into measurable, time-boxed experiments and a repeatable rollout pattern that product, infra, and SRE can own together.

Scope (what this doc covers)
- Cross-team experiment slate for Q3 2026 focused on: request-latency SLOs (p95, p99 tail), error-rate SLOs, and warm-cache availability for hosted endpoints.
- Quick-runbook updates and an ops checklist for canary rollouts.
- Communication and escalation flows for degraded SLOs.
- NOT in scope: major architectural refactors (separate RFC).

Primary goals
- Reduce p99 latency of chat-generation route by 20% under 95th-percentile traffic pattern for the next 90 days.
- Reduce user-visible errors (5xx + failed streaming) by 35% for Dedicated customers in EU region within two sprints.
- Establish 2 reproducible experiments that yield unit-cost-neutral latency improvements (batching + KV-ttl tuning).

Stakeholders and roles
- Product: Priya Nair (owner for Hosted API product commitments)
- SRE: Maya Chen (program lead) + on-call rotations (see below)
- Serving runtime eng: Diego Alvarez (experiment impl, perf instrumentation)
- Infrastructure: Evan Ross (scaling/autoscaler rules + capacity changes)
- Solutions/CS: Sabrina Li (customer comms + impact triage)
- Security & Compliance: FYI and signoff for any new telemetry collection

Meeting cadence
- Weekly experiment standup (Thu 10:30am PT) — owners report progress, blockers, and churn on telemetry.
- Postmortem sync (ad-hoc within 48h after high-severity incident) — define immediate mitigations.
- Pre-canary readiness review (48h before rollout) — checklist signoff from SRE + runtime + infra.

Experiment slate (prioritized)
1) KV-cache TTL staged tuning (small risk, quick rollback)
   - Hypothesis: increasing prefix/KV cache TTL for common completion prefixes reduces upstream model compute and cuts p99 for short-chat requests.
   - Owner: Diego
   - Steps: (A) instrument per-prefix hit-rate; (B) create two TTL cohorts (30s, 90s) on a small % of traffic; (C) compare p95/p99 and cost per token.
   - Measurement queries: promQL examples in linked ticket (JIRA-REL-4123).
   - Success criteria: p99 drop >=12% on cohort with no >1% increase in cold-start failure.

2) Adaptive batching experiment (medium risk, requires runtime change)
   - Hypothesis: aggressive micro-batching during backpressure windows reduces p99 latency and amortizes per-token GPU overhead.
   - Owner: Diego + Serving Runtime
   - Steps: implement batch-size cap + dynamic delay window, throttle policy for low-latency routes only. Canary on non-enterprise routes.
   - Success criteria: >15% p99 reduction and <5% increase in p95 (no user-visible regressions).

3) Autoscaler hysteresis tuning in EU region (low-medium risk)
   - Hypothesis: current scale-down is too aggressive causing bursty cold starts — add 60s additional hysteresis and grace CPU cushion.
   - Owner: Evan
   - Steps: modify k8s/autoscaler config for dedicated pools, run 1-week pilot during off-peak, observe cold-start rate.
   - Success criteria: cold-start incidents drop by 40% without >10% extra reserved capacity spend.

4) Route-level circuit breaker and fast-fail rollout (higher risk)
   - Hypothesis: early fast-fail for overloaded downstream services reduces cascading failures and keeps dominant error-mode transparent to clients.
   - Owner: Maya + Diego
   - Steps: implement soft-fail thresholds, monitor for false positives, rollback plan if customer complaints >X.
   - Success criteria: overall system error-rate reduces and downstream queue sizes stabilize.

Operational runbook changes (quick wins)
- Add a short checklist for pre-canary: (a) telemetry dashboards up-to-date, (b) rollback playbook reviewed, (c) pagers aware, (d) customer-impact matrix reviewed.
- Short-runbook: how to revert KV TTL changes and how to scale Dedicated pools manually.
- Update on-call runbook with new Prometheus alerts (p99-surge, sustained-inflight-requests).

Measurement plan and telemetry
- Baseline window: last 30 days of production traffic (use 2026-06-10 to 2026-07-10 as initial window).
- Dashboards to update: model-serving-latency (p50/p95/p99), prefix-cache-hit-rate, cold-start-rate, downstream-queue-length, per-customer-error-rate.
- Instrumentation additions: cost-per-request tag, route-level bucketed-latency histograms.

Canary & rollout pattern
- 3-phase rollout: 1) internal-only (10% internal engineers), 2) opt-in developer-tier (5% of external devs), 3) broad roll (50% then 100%) with pause points.
- Pre-rollback thresholds: specified per experiment (tied to success criteria above).
- Communication: post to #reliability-ops and update the Hosted API status page during phases.

Risk register (top items)
- Regressions for enterprise customers — mitigation: canary exclusion list + dedicated rollback path.
- Telemetry blind spots (not enough cardinality) — mitigation: instrument before expanding cohorts.
- Cost churn if experiments cause more GPU usage — mitigation: cost monitoring + autoscaling holdback.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Q1: Should Dedicated EU pools be excluded from the first KV-ttl cohort? (Priya to decide by 2026-07-20)
- Q2: Threshold for customer-impact alarm that triggers immediate rollback (options: 0.5% error increase vs absolute 5xx count)
- Q3: Does Security want sampling enabled for extra traces? (Security to weigh in)

Deliverables and schedule (8-week horizon)
- Week 0 (kickoff): confirm owners, baseline dashboards, create experiment tickets (owner: Maya).
- Week 1–2: implement instrumentation + small internal cohort KV-ttl test.
- Week 3–4: adaptive batching canary on 10% traffic; autoscaler hysteresis pilot in EU test pool.
- Week 5: sync with customer success, review canary telemetry.
- Week 6–7: expand promising experiments to opt-in developer cohort, prepare runbook changes.
- Week 8: decision point — roll to broad or fall back. Write short paper (1–2 pages) summarizing results and recommended permanent changes.

Acceptance criteria for the program
- Clear documented before/after telemetry showing SLOs improved per the goal numbers.
- Runbooks updated and onboarded to on-call rotations.
- A rollback mechanism validated and rehearsed.
- Executive summary for product + platform with explicit cost delta.

Artifacts to produce
- Experiment ticket set (linked), canary manifest snippets, updated Grafana dashboards, one-page exec summary, runbook diff PR.

Notes (scratchpad style)
- early notes: customer X saw repeated p99 spikes on 2026-06-29 — likely autoscale behavior + model cold init.
- keep experiments small; prefer iterative expansion over big-bang.
- measure cost per successful completion (we have instrumentation but needs route tag).

Next steps (this week)
- Maya: create experiment epics + invite Diego, Evan, Priya to kick kickoff meeting.
- Diego: prototype cache-hit instrumentation and share promQL samples.
- Evan: snapshot current autoscaler config and cost baseline.
- Priya: list customer cohorts to exclude/include for canaries.

Unresolved followups
- Add a small UX note for SDKs about transient error behavior if circuit-breaker fast-fail is enabled.
- Confirm whether we can safely add cost-per-request tag for billing telemetry without PII concerns.
